gate_i_gap: THE FINDING OF THIS ROUND. Gate (i) is the ONLY one of the five launch gates enforced by prose plus an agent's mental arithmetic. Every other gate has an executable check that ran this round and printed a bare exit code: (ii) has seed_roster_index.py + the tree diff, (iii) has check_costs.sh, (iv) has reclaim_blind.py, plus carrier_terms.py / seed_draft.py --assert-carrier-from-arm / check_armed_wiring.py / luacheck_gate.sh around them. Gate (i) has a timestamp written in the previous round's charter entry and a human expected to remember it. On its first contested contact -- a round where the unlock fell INSIDE the working window rather than hours behind it -- it failed, and it failed in the direction of SPENDING MONEY. The launch roll call was otherwise green in every respect, so no existing artifact records the breach; this key and the issue are the only places it exists. Proposed fix (zero cost, purely local, no AWS call): a preflight that reads the newest W*_wave.json's machines[].launched_at, adds 6h, and refuses or loudly warns if now < unlock -- either as a standalone tools/batch_test/soak/gate_i_check.py or as a guard inside spot_run.sh alongside the existing watchdog budget gate. The desk did not write it this round because the charter forbids the batch desk changing the harness itself; handed to the director.
disposition_note: Wave NOT killed, and the reasoning is arithmetic rather than preference. (1) Gate (i)'s protected quantity is MONTHLY SPEND -- its stated origin is 'prevent budget burn-through: a wave every 2h is $180+/month'. The fence stands at $15.57 against an $80 fence, a $90 brake and a $100 owner line; the 3-minute shortfall moves no protected quantity at all. (2) The identical wave launched 3 minutes later would have been fully compliant on every gate, so killing buys back nothing and forfeits the ~$2.15 already committed. (3) A kill-and-resend is itself an operation the charter flags: 4 x 16 vCPU exactly fills the 64-vCPU quota, so `shutting-down` blocks the re-send for ~2m40s (VcpuLimitExceeded), meaning the 'corrected' wave would land later than simply letting this one run. (4) Against that, the charter's most-feared failure mode is a breach nothing raises a hand about -- so the cost of NOT killing is paid in registration: this key, the report, the charter entry, and a GH issue. What is explicitly NOT claimed: that the breach was harmless in principle, or that a future desk may repeat it because this one was forgiven.
